items.source_en:
Ice Hockey stick, used on Taris in the city of Edmonton, Canada, during a 1988 championship game.

Ice Hockey is a contact sport played on an ice rink where two teams with five players and two goal tenders, called "goalies" compete to deposit a rubberized "puck" in the other team's goal. The players traverse the rink on specialized shoes mounted on thin metal blades, called ice skates, and manipulate the puck with specialized curved sticks such as the one displayed here.

Engineering gravitational folds, "pulling" the far side of the solar system closer to us? It's all going to be possible.

items.source_en:
Truth is, the origins of hyperspace travel are as mysterious as the galaxy itself. The ancient Rakata were the first to unlock its secrets, using techniques and tools we still barely understand. Their methods seemed to rely on something innate to their species—an ability to sense and manipulate hyperspace in ways no modern technology can replicate.

For the rest of the galaxy, the path to mastering hyperspace required a different approach. Early pioneers turned to nature, observing the majestic Purrgil—massive, whale-like creatures capable of traveling through hyperspace with astonishing precision. By studying their behavior and patterns, researchers began to develop the first mechanical systems that mimicked these natural navigators.

Today, hyperdrive technology is so ubiquitous that we rarely think about its origins. Yet, every jump through hyperspace is a reminder of the ingenuity—and the mysteries—behind this galaxy-spanning achievement.

[Professor Hosh Venn’s Foundations of Hyperspace Navigation remains the definitive work on the hyperdrive, chronicling the ancient Rakatan breakthroughs, the influence of Purrgil studies, and the evolution of the technology that connects us all.]

사실 초공간 도약 여행의 기원은 우리 은하계 자체만큼이나 여전히 베일에 싸여 있습니다. 고대 라카타 문명은 우리가 오늘날까지도 거의 이해하지 못하는 기술과 도구들을 사용하여 초공간의 비밀을 가장 먼저 풀어낸 선구자였습니다. 그들의 방식은 종족 고유의 선천적인 자질, 즉 현대 기술로는 도저시 흉내 낼 수 없는 방식으로 초공간을 감지하고 조율하는 능력에 크게 의존했던 것으로 보입니다.

그 외 은하계의 다른 종족들이 초공간을 정복하기 위해서는 전혀 다른 접근법이 필요했습니다. 초기의 개척자들은 눈을 돌려 대자연을 관찰하기 시작했습니다. 그들은 초공간을 놀라울 정도로 정밀하게 유영하는 거대하고 웅장한 고래를 닮은 생명체, '퍼길'에 주목했습니다. 퍼길의 행동 양식과 이동 패턴을 꼼꼼히 탐구한 끝에, 과학자들은 마침내 이 자연의 길잡이들을 모방한 최초의 기계식 초공간 도약 장치를 개발해 낼 수 있었습니다.

오늘날 초공간 추진기 기술은 숨 쉬는 공기처럼 도처에 널려 있어 그 기원을 깊이 생각하는 이가 거의 없습니다. 그러나 우리가 초공간을 관통해 도약하는 그 매 순간은, 온 은하를 하나로 묶어준 이 위대한 위업의 이면에 숨겨진 인류의 지혜와 깊은 신비를 일깨워 줍니다.

[호쉬 벤 교수의 저서 '초공간 항법의 기초'는 고대 라카타의 비약적인 도약, 퍼길 연구가 남긴 영향, 그리고 우리 모두를 연결해 준 추진기 기술의 진화 과정을 기록한 가장 권위 있는 학술서로 굳건히 자리 잡았습니다.]

locations.vanilla_source_en:
[An excerpt from the highly acclaimed novel, "Fields of Everglass," set in the near-future during a fictional wartime era.]

...And yet, Tal'at did not back down. "No sir, I won't fire on them. Regardless of what you say they did, those soldiers were once like us. They're our family. We have no reason to fight them."

This impressed Florence. Was Tal'at really willing to put everything on the line just to protect her compatriots? She knew the war was ridiculous, but to see him face his commander now and absolutely refuse a direct order, knowing that it could amount to treason. This was the same Tal'at, who no more than a week ago had carried out an order to ambush and lock up her entire squad. She knew there was a gentleness to the man, but until now she had not been able to know for sure just how reasonable he could be.

"You're out of line, soldier! You want to think about what you're doing and run that by me one more time?" Commander Greeson barked. Spittle flew. His face was turning bright red with anger. Greeson was not accustomed to disobedience. 

"You heard me. I'm not repeating myself." Tal'at looked over to Florence. He knew the gravity of the situation, but she had taught him so much about this unjust war in their few short days together, that in this moment, he decided even if it cost him gravely, he would do the right thing. As he noticed the other officers begin to shuffle uncomfortably, noting a break in their resolve, a smirk crossed his face. The cracks began to show. He knew the tide was about to turn, and that his small act of defiance could be the one to usher in the end of this foolish conflict...
